Q: favicon.png vs favicon.ico - why should I use PNG instead of ICO? A:

Some social tools like Google+ use a simple method to get a favicon for external links, fetching http://your.domainname.com/favicon.ico

Since they don't prefetch the HTML content, the <link> tag will not work. In this case, you might want to use a mod_rewrite rule or just place the file in the default location.

Q: Appending information to Outlook email A:

Here's the fix — Word's Range object gives you InsertBefore and InsertAfter methods, which do exactly what you're after without needing to manipulate the body as a plain string:

Set oOutlookEditor = .GetInspector.WordEditor
oOutlookEditor.Content.Paste
oOutlookEditor.Content.InsertBefore String_Greeting & vbCrLf & vbCrLf
oOutlookEditor.Content.InsertAfter vbCrLf & vbCrLf & String_Closing

Why this works:

  • oOutlookEditor.Content is a Range object representing the entire email body — it behaves like a live "window" onto the document, not a static string.

  • .Paste inserts your Word doc's clipboard content into that range.

  • InsertBefore and InsertAfter are Range methods that add text immediately before/after the range's current boundaries — effectively giving you the String_Greeting & .Body & String_Closing behavior you wanted, just expressed through the object model instead of string concatenation.

  • Because Content auto-expands to cover the full document after each insertion, you don't need to manually recalculate range positions.

Updated relevant section of your loop:

.To = RecipientEmail
.Subject = SubjectLine & " - test " & MailCounter - 1 & " minute send"

Set oOutlookEditor = .GetInspector.WordEditor
oOutlookEditor.Content.Paste
oOutlookEditor.Content.InsertBefore String_Greeting & vbCrLf & vbCrLf
oOutlookEditor.Content.InsertAfter vbCrLf & vbCrLf & String_Closing

.DeferredDeliveryTime = DateAdd("n", 20, Now)
.Send

A few things worth cleaning up while you're in there:

  1. .Body = Test — this line references an undeclared variable Test, which will throw a compile error (or silently insert an empty string if Option Explicit isn't set). Remove it; the .Paste line replaces its purpose.

  2. .Display before .Send — fine for debugging, but if you're sending in bulk, consider removing it once you've confirmed the merge logic works, since displaying every Inspector window can slow down the loop and steal focus repeatedly.

  3. Set olApp = New Outlook.Application inside the loop — this creates a new Outlook Application instance on every iteration, which is unnecessary overhead. Move this line above the For loop so it's only instantiated once.

  4. Formatting fidelity: InsertBefore/InsertAfter insert plain text, which will inherit the character formatting from that Range position — fine for simple greetings/closings, but if you need specific fonts or bold/italic styling, format the inserted Range's .Font object right after insertion, e.g.:

    Dim oRange As ObjectSet oRange = oOutlookEditor.Range(0, 0)oRange.InsertBefore String_Greeting & vbCrLf & vbCrLfoRange.Font.Bold = True

Q: Microsoft Visual C++ 2022 X86 Minimum Runtime Error (Redlist14, specifically vc_runtimeMinimum_x86.msi) During Installation A:

Looks like that your computer is missing a required component of the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime library. For this issue, here are some suggestions to troubleshoot:

  1. Download, run this tool, select Uninstalling, try to uninstall following runtimes.
Microsoft Visual C++ xxxx Xxx Additional Runtime – xx.xx.xxxxx

Microsoft Visual C++ xxxx Xxx Debug Runtime – xx.xx.xxxxx

Microsoft Visual C++ xxxx Xxx Minimum Runtime – xx.xx.xxxxx

  1. Download and reinstall the Visual C++ Redistributable package from here.

  2. Run Visual Studio Installer as administrator and try to repair your VS.

  3. If not work, you can also collect setup log files generated during installation and then search detailed error messages to analyze the cause of the issue.

    (1) download Microsoft Visual Studio and .NET Framework log collection tool https://aka.ms/vscollect

    (2) run Collect.exe in an administrative command prompt The tool generates a vslogs.zip file in your %TEMP% folder, typically at C:\Users\YourName\AppData\Local\Temp\vslogs.zip.

    For more information, please refer to: Troubleshoot installation or upgrades - Visual Studio (Windows)

Q: Using jq with Jenkins pipeline A:

This was solved by writing a helper function that uses the JsonSurplerClassic() to convert the string to json.

def make_json(string_val){
   def jsonmaker = new JsonSlurperClassic()
   def jsonval = jsonmaker.parseText(string_val)
   println jsonval.getClass()
   return jsonval
}

Notes:

  • This helper is using JsonSlurperClassic() as it creates a hashmap and avoids the jenkins NotSerializableException exception if we use the JsonSurpler()
  • Secondly calling this helper solved the jenkins exception error rather than writing it inside the withAWS... block.

Following worked :

withAWS(credentials: aws_env_credential){
    efs_details = sh(
    script: "aws efs describe-file-systems --region='${aws_region_for_cluster}' | jq --arg efs_name ${efs_name} '.[] | .[] | select(.Name==$efs_name)'",
    encoding: 'UTF-8',
    returnStdout: true
    )
    efs_details_json = make_json(efs_details)
    }

Can now use the dot operators,

efs_details_json.name
efs_details_json.OwnerId
...

Hope this helps other(me in future) to save time for more non-trivial items.

Q: passing values using hivevar in HIVE A:

You need to put the string in single quotes for it to parse correctly as a string inside the sql after interpolation.

hive -hivevar sys_nm="'This is a param'" -e 'select * from rd_sys where rd_sys_nm=${hivevar:sys_nm}'

Q: In Azure DevOps, link manual test cases with automated test scripts using PowerShell Pester Framework and CI/CD Pipeline A:

You should take a look at the Cross-Platform Test Result Publisher which can publish test results from many different test formats against a Test Plan. (disclosure: I'm the author of the extension)

The extension supports a variety of strategies to link your test automation results to the Test Cases. Given that the names of your Pester names match the names of the Test Case automation, you should be able to publish without modification to your tests.

- task: PublishTestPlanResults@1
  inputs:
    testResultFormat: nunit
    testResultFiles: PesterReport/TestResults.xml
    testPlan: '180' # you can also specify the name of Test Plan if you'd prefer
    testRunTitle: 'Test Plan Results'
    #testCaseMatchStrategy: 'name' # matches against the name of the Test Case

The testCaseMatchStrategy supports different ways to establish the relationship between your test automation and the Test Cases. The default value is auto which will use all of the strategies until it finds one that works, in your case the name strategy looks at case insensitive matches between test automation names and Test Case titles.

Full syntax for the extension is here
